headline: COP31 Concludes Without Final Agreement After Record-Breaking Talks
metaDescription: The UN climate conference COP31 has ended without a consensus on a final text after surpassing the record for the longest summit in the event's history.
aiSummaryBullets: The COP31 climate summit officially ended without an agreement on a final text after two weeks of negotiations.
The conference became the longest in history, extending 44 hours beyond its scheduled conclusion time.
The European Union and Panama were among those who rejected the draft, citing the omission of language regarding fossil fuels.
aiContextParagraph: The COP31 climate conference, which took place over the course of two weeks, concluded on November 22, 2026, without a formal agreement. Originally scheduled to finish on Friday, November 20, the event extended into the weekend, ultimately surpassing the duration record previously held by COP25 in Madrid in 2019. Reports indicate that the final collapse of negotiations occurred after several nations, including members of the European Union and Panama, refused to sign a proposed document. The primary point of contention cited by these parties was the lack of specific provisions addressing the phase-out of fossil fuels within the agreement text. This failure to reach a consensus marks a significant moment for the UN-led climate process, as participants were unable to bridge the gap between varying national positions on environmental policy targets before officially ending the extended summit session.
whyItIsViral: The event is trending due to its status as the longest climate conference in history and the significant failure to reach a final agreement, covered by two major national outlets.
